Sam L: Quick question - I turned 50 this year. How do catch-up contributions work for 401(k) and HSA? Can I do both, and do I need to notify payroll separately for the 401(k) catch-up?

Nina (People Ops): Congrats Sam! Short answers: yes you can contribute catch-up to your 401(k) if you're 50+, and HSA has its own contribution limits but no "catch-up" unless you're 55+ and using HSA for retiree medical? Actually HSA does allow an extra $1,000 catch-up if you're 55 or older (spousal rules apply). For 401(k) catch-up you need to change your deferral election (usually a separate election in the payroll portal).

Carlos (Payroll): To add to Nina: we support automatic 401(k) catch-up via ADP. Use the PAY-401K-CATCH payroll code and submit the elective change in Workday > Benefits > Retirement elections. If you want us to manual-enter for mid-cycle, DM me.

Sam L: If I enable catch-up mid-year, is the match calculated on the catch-up amount?

Nina (People Ops): Per plan rules, the employer match is applied to eligible deferrals up to the IRS limit components the plan uses. Typically catch-up contributions (age-based additional deferrals) are NOT matched by the employer. Our plan administrator (SecureRetire) follows that standard. You can see the SPD for exact wording: https://benefits.redwood.com/401k/spd.pdf

Carlos (Payroll): Confirmed: we code catch-up deferrals as 401K-CATCH (post-tax or pre-tax depending on your election). Payroll excludes 401K-CATCH from the match calculation in the payroll feed to SecureRetire.

Sam L: What about FSA? I currently have a dependent care FSA and a limited-purpose FSA. Does catch-up or HSA contributions affect my FSA limits?

Nina (People Ops): FSAs are separate buckets. Limited-purpose FSA is designed to work with HSA (it only covers dental/vision/eligible limited items). HSA contributions don't reduce your FSA eligibility. However, you cannot contribute to a general-purpose FSA if you have an HSA-eligible HDHP (that would make you ineligible for the HSA). If you already have a limited-purpose FSA, you're fine.

Sam L: Timeline question: I want catch-up to start next pay period. What's the cutoff to submit?

Carlos (Payroll): Submit the change by EOD Tuesday to take effect on the next pay period. If it's after payroll cutoff we'll do it the following cycle. For catch-up we need the election form plus the age verification (usually a DOB on file is fine).

Nina (People Ops): FYI open enrollment note: Catch-up elections are allowed outside open enrollment because they're age-based changes. HSA/FSA elections follow open enrollment rules unless you have a qualifying life event. Online help: https://benefits.redwood.com/faq#catchup

Benefits Bot: Reminder: 401(k) catch-up contribution limit for 2026 is $7,500. HSA catch-up (age 55+) is $1,000. See IRS notices and plan docs.

Sam L: Thanks team. Last: if I move part of my pre-tax 401(k) to Roth this year, will that affect catch-up?

Nina (People Ops): You can split your deferrals between pre-tax and Roth; catch-up itself is a separate add-on and follows same pre/post-tax election options per plan rules. Employer match is still made on eligible deferrals (not catch-up) and is contributed pre-tax to the 401(k) account. If you want a run of projected year-end numbers, Carlos can run a demo calc.

Carlos (Payroll): Happy to run numbers. DM me your current deferral %, salary, and desired catch-up %, I'll simulate match and year-to-date totals.

Sam L: Appreciate it :party_parrot:
